previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to fluid overload, presenting with worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. Despite medication adherence, dietary challenges contributed to the decompensation. He was treated with IV and oral diuretics, including a trial of metolazone, which improved fluid status but caused transient worsening of kidney function. A diuretic holiday was implemented, after which therapy was resumed successfully. His breathing improved, and he was transitioned to oral torsemide at a reduced dose. Paroxysmal atrial tachycardia was noted on ICD interrogation, prompting initiation of warfarin for stroke prevention, with INR 1.8 at discharge. A urine culture grew coagulase-negative staph, deemed contaminant. Repeat imaging ruled out pneumonia. He was discharged home with close follow-up, medication reconciliation, and instructions on weight monitoring and dietary compliance.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Acute on chronic CHF exacerbation: Pt presented with dyspnea, 
weight gain (approximately 10 lb since discharge on ___, 
elevated JVP, and ___ edema.  His BNP was 6619.  His chest xray 
showed evidence of pulmonary edema.  Likely triggers included a 
UTI and excess fluid intake. Pt got 140 mg furosemide in the ED. 
 His O2 saturation is 99% NC.  When he arrived on the floor, he 
received another 140 mg IV furosemide bolus.  He was then 
started on a furosemide drip at 10 mg/hr.  He diuresed very well 
and on ___ his furosemide drip was decreased to 5 mg/hr.  He 
was also started on dobutamine 2.5 mcg/kg/min drip given an 
elevated lactate and LFTs and concern for poor perfusion.  
Patient's isosorbide mononitrate was fractionated to isosorbide 
dinitrate (uptitrated during hospitalization) and hydralazine 
was also uptitrated. He was maintained on metoprolol.  He was 
also started on losartan 12.5 mg per day. Patient became 
hypotensive and tachycardic on ___, at which time dobutamine 
was discontinued with normalization of vital signs. Cr increased 
on ___ and diuretics were held, PO intake was encouraged, and 
Cr improved. Patient was transitioned to PO Torsemide 140mg 
daily on ___. Discharge weight 133.6kg.

 He was treated with a five day ceftriaxone course (1 g IV Q24H,

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is patent
with hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 11.4 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 11.0 cm. The left kidney measures 11.9 cm.
Normal cortical echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation is seen
bilaterally. There is no evidence of masses, stones, or hydronephrosis in the
kidneys.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Unremarkable abdominal ultrasound.
